value: This article introduces allegories, a class of categories designed to provide a foundational categorical calculus of relations, mirroring properties found in the category of relations (`Rel`) over a regular category. An allegory is defined as a locally posetal 2-category equipped with an involution, binary meets in its hom-posets, and satisfying the modular law. The framework generalizes concepts traditionally handled by functional language, offering smooth approaches to constructions like regular and exact completions. Different types of allegories, such as tabular, division, and power allegories, are shown to be equivalent to various logical and foundational categories like regular categories, Heyting categories, and topoi, respectively, highlighting their role in internalizing logic and supporting existential quantification within a relational setting.
